lines: A sequencer that walks a binary tree of nodes, one node per clock, taking a branch at random wherever a node has two children
In Step trigger type this steps the sequence in the same way the clock does; in Sequence trigger type it picks a fresh path through the whole tree and starts it at the root
Moves to the next node on each rising edge, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Returns to the root node on a rising edge, and the clock is ignored for 1ms afterwards
A 1ms pulse at 10V each time a path through the tree finishes
The active node's number as a pitch, one twelfth of a volt per number, so node 1 gives 0V and node 13 gives 1V
Shifts the chance at every node in the tree, -1 to +1; turned up the second branch becomes more likely, turned down the first branch does
Adds to the CHANCE MOD knob, 1V covering half of its travel
Stops the gate and the clock stepping the sequence, so the active node keeps sending
Flips the HOLD button on each rising edge
Turns the sequence round at the end of a path so it walks back towards the root, in place of jumping straight to it
Flips the BOUNCE button on each rising edge
Chooses Step, where each clock takes a branch at random as it arrives, or Sequence, where a whole path is chosen in advance and the clock walks along it
Flips the TRIG TYPE button on each rising edge
A 1ms pulse at 10V while the active node carries this jack's number

Note — drag the screen to move around the tree and scroll on it to zoom; the three buttons under the screen follow the active node, undo an edit and redo it, and none can be clicked for help

Note — a new Treequencer holds a root node and two children, so it sequences from the moment a clock is patched

lines: An oscillator built from three points on a sphere, each turned by its own sine LFO, with the points flattened onto a plane to make the output

Adds to that axis's INFLUENCE knob, 1V covering the whole of its travel, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Adds a steady turn of that axis on top of whatever its LFO is doing, 0 to 100
Adds to that axis's ROTATION knob, 1V for each step of its 0 to 100 scale
Raises that axis's LFO by whole octaves; set to Off the axis is pinned to 1Hz under the Old dephase algorithm and stops turning altogether under the New one
Adds to that axis's OCTAVE knob at 1V per octave
Sets how far that axis's LFO turns the sphere, none at the far left and its full amount at the far right

Cycles the number of voices the two outputs carry, 1 to 16, each voice a slightly turned copy of the sphere; right-click it to choose a number directly
Cycles Mono, where both outputs carry the same signal, Full Stereo, where points near the centre of the sphere are sent to both sides, and Sides, where a point only reaches the side it lies on
The left side of the flattened sphere, one polyphonic channel per spread voice; in Mono it carries the same signal as the other output
The right side of the flattened sphere, one polyphonic channel per spread voice; in Mono it carries the same signal as the other output
Note — setting all three V/OCT jacks to the same pitch moves the pitch while holding the shape of the rotation you have built
Note — turning one axis moves the other two, so the three never act on their own
Note — the screen draws the path each of the three points has traced, one colour per axis, faded down by that axis's INFLUENCE knob
Menu — Projection Axis: X, Y, Z — chooses the plane the three points are flattened onto to make the output
Menu — Disable Spread Volume Normalization — stops the output being divided down as the spread count rises, so more voices give a louder sum; once off it reads Enable
Menu — Dephase Algorithm: Old, New — Old pulls each LFO back towards zero phase, New drives each towards the phase a free-running oscillator of that frequency would have reached
Menu — Sample Rate: Full, Half — Half runs the oscillator on every second sample
Menu — Enable Quantization — right-click an OCTAVE knob; makes that knob snap to whole octaves again, and it reads Disable Quantization while snapping is on

quatosc.notes: Read from the source at tag v2.1.14 (commit 75e5f70), which is the installed build. Input 3 (TRIGGER, named Gate) is configured but has no PortWidget and is never read, so it gets no line, no tag and no props. Param 14 (Dephase Algorithm) likewise has no widget; it is reachable only from the panel menu and is covered by a Menu line. The maker's page says setting an OCTAVE knob to Off disables that LFO; in the code calcVOctFreq returns 1.f for a negative octave under the Old dephase algorithm, which leaves that axis turning at 1Hz, and 0.f under the New one. Under the New algorithm a Z octave below zero also forces the Z LFO influence to a fixed 0.95 (line 325). The three ROTATION jacks are given no range because the knob they add to runs 0 to 100 and the sum is never clamped, so no single voltage span is the fact.

lines: A module with no controls of its own, whose purpose is to put a Night-bin button on Rack's menu bar for fetching nightly builds of plugins from GitHub
Note — the panel carries nothing that can be clicked; everything the module does is on the Night-bin button it adds to Rack's own menu bar, and removing the module removes the button
Note — a plugin can be checked only if it publishes its source on GitHub and has a release tagged Nightly holding a .vcvplugin file for your operating system and processor
Note — a downloaded build is written into Rack's plugins folder and takes effect at the next restart of Rack
Note — a red dot on the Night-bin button means an update was found, and the button's text reports progress while it is querying or downloading
Note — the plugin's settings, including the access token in plain text and the list of plugins to check, are kept in questionablemodules.json in Rack's user folder
Menu — Add / Remove Modules — on the Night-bin button in Rack's menu bar; lists every installed plugin, and clicking one adds it to the list that is checked or takes it off
Menu — Add All Plugins — inside Add / Remove Modules on the Night-bin button in Rack's menu bar; adds every plugin that names a GitHub source, and appears only once a token has been entered
Menu — Query for Updates — on the Night-bin button in Rack's menu bar; checks each chosen plugin's GitHub repository for a Nightly release newer than the installed build
Menu — Github Access Token — on the Night-bin button in Rack's menu bar; a text field for a GitHub personal access token, which raises the limit GitHub puts on unauthenticated requests
Menu — Clear Github Access Token — on the Night-bin button in Rack's menu bar; deletes the stored token, and replaces the text field once a token has been entered
Menu — Update All — on the Night-bin button in Rack's menu bar; downloads every update the last query found
nightbin.notes: Read from the source at tag v2.1.14 (commit 75e5f70), which is the installed build. The module declares no parameters, inputs or outputs, so it has no tags and no props; all of its behaviour is on the button it inserts into Rack's menu bar (nightbin.cpp:500-512), and the menu lines say so. The module sends HTTP requests to api.github.com on a background thread as soon as it is placed and whenever a query is asked for (nightbin.cpp:77, 306). The token the user types is stored unencrypted in questionablemodules.json under gitPersonalAccessToken (nightbin.cpp:361); no token value appears anywhere in this entry.

Note — bypassing the module leaves the rack's own background showing

Menu — Add Custom Color — inside Change Color; a name field and red, green and blue sliders that repaint the background as you drag; Save keeps the colour for every patch, Clear returns to Green

greenscreen.notes: Read from the source at tag v2.1.14 (commit 75e5f70), which is the installed build. The theme menu is left out of every other module in this plugin as plugin-wide decoration, but here the colour menu is the module, so it is written out. The maker's page says the three jacks take -10V to 10V for -100 to 100 per cent and are added as offsets; the code takes the voltage divided by ten, adds it, then takes the absolute value of the fractional part, so the colour wraps past full rather than clamping and a negative voltage folds back up instead of subtracting. The jacks are declared with a custom port widget that draws nothing and refuses drags, tooltips and its own menu while Toggle CV Inputs is off (greenscreen.cpp:414-443), so they exist in the census but cannot be used until that item is switched on. Colour changes are smoothed towards the target rather than applied at once (line 573-575).

smute.notes: Read from the source at tag v2.1.14 (commit 75e5f70), which is the installed build. The mute button and the ratio knob of a row share one centre: the button (a CKD6 at 28px scaled to 0.85) sits inside the knob (36px scaled to 1.085), so a click on the dark inner circle reaches the button and a click on the ringed outer edge reaches the knob. Help.cpp resolves overlapping controls by the smaller box, so both are reachable and both are tagged. The panel prints no label on the knob at all; it is called Ratio in the maker's tooltip and on the maker's page, and the lines use that name. Ratio values map through a 65-entry list, /32 at -32 through Immediate at 0 to X32 at +32.
